response.headline: No single cause dominates this zone; a capacity strain across many people is the most likely contributor [capacity_strain][zone_overview].

causes.explanation: 7,108 people are in cells where only 1-2 operators are identified within 5 km [zone_overview], yet the zone average is 2.7 operators nearby, so operator scarcity is not universal [zone_overview].

The zone carries a capacity-strain signal across 22,126 people and speeds fell 55% from the oldest to the latest quarter [zone_overview], but the rule-based fix notes no single weakness dominates and the evidence is zone-level rather than cell-specific [fix_rule].
No single weakness dominates the zone's cells and the rule-based fix is to gather measurements first [fix_rule], so the evidence cannot separate the likely causes at this point.

fix_plan.why: The rule-based fix is to gather measurements first because no single weakness dominates the zone's cells [fix_rule]; the zone-level signals (capacity strain across 22,126 people, speeds down 55%, 19,216 below half the local reference median, 40,407 with 30%+ speed falls, 7,108 with only 1-2 operators nearby) cannot yet be separated into cell-specific causes [zone_overview].
assumptions: line of sight to cell centres, not a radio model
measurements are needed before choosing add_operators, capacity_upgrade, or new_site

review.reason: The plan correctly treats this as an improvement opportunity (not a gap), cites the zone's specific weaknesses from [zone_overview] (capacity strain, speed drops, below-median speeds, limited operators), matches the fix_type 'gather_data' to the rule [fix_rule] which states no single weakness dominates, states assumptions, and does not claim 'no service' or 'no coverage'.
